correctness.rationale: For independent uniform-arclength vertices on the hyperbolic radius-R geodesic circle, polar angles are iid uniform and cyclic gap density is 1/(2π²). The hyperbolic cosine law yields the exact sign factor 4s²sin(u/2)sin(w/2)[cos(v/2)+s²sin(u/2)sin(w/2)], s=sinh R. Only one gap may exceed π. The (t,x) Jacobian 2 and allowed |x|<acos(κ cos t), κ=1+2/s², give the conversion 6J(κ)/π², with J'(κ)=−atanh(1/κ)/κ and J=(Li₂(z)−Li₂(−z))/2 for z=1/κ. This proves P=1/4+3(Li₂(z)−Li₂(−z))/π², strict increase and the stated R↓0/R→∞ asymptotics. Independently integrated J and dilog series at R=.35,1,2.4 with error below 10⁻³⁶; finite quadrature does not prove the all-radius theorem. Curvature −1, intrinsic angles and circle-boundary arclength sampling are essential.
